PHILIPPINES:  Tropical Update

Hurricane/Typhoon/Cyclone Updates & Information  continues monitoring the Western Pacific as a low-pressure area, 99W, is slowly organizing. One of these systems has the potential to develop into the next named tropical cyclone: #DomengPH (Philippines name) / #Jangmi (international name).

---- Neither PAGASA or JTWC have yet to designate this LOW PRESSURE AREA.

Residents across the Philippines are encouraged to closely monitor weather updates during the upcoming week of May 27–31, 2026, as conditions are likely to support the development of a TROPICAL STORM — with a TYPHOON increasingly certain by May 30-31, 2026.  At the moment, steering currents are likely to keep this system east of the Philippines without a LANDFALL; however, we must monitor the possible development and track closely this week.

While it is still too early to determine an exact track or intensity, interests in Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao should stay alert for possible heavy rainfall, gusty winds, flooding, rough seas, and changing forecast conditions.
Please continue checking this page daily for the latest tropical updates, forecasts, satellite analysis, and potential impacts as the situation develops. Stay prepared and stay safe. 🌀

Roshin

🚨The Scenario: "The Quorum Trap"🚨

🇵🇭Phase 1: The Tactical Arrests

Days before the final verdict vote in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, the executive branch or a lower court issues arrest warrants for four core senators of the pro-Duterte bloc (reducing their active front from 13 down to 9). Following the De Lima precedent, the courts strictly deny them bail and refuse to grant them remote electronic voting privileges, declaring that criminal arrest does not constitute force majeure.

🇵🇭Phase 2: The Plenary Stand-Off

The Senate convenes to vote on the Articles of Impeachment. The anti-Duterte faction believes they have a clear path to victory because the opposition’s numbers are severely depleted.

Total active senators in the room: 20 (11 anti-Duterte, 9 pro-Duterte allies).

The 4 arrested senators are physically absent.

🇵🇭Phase 3: The "Total Seats" Constitutional Wall

Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano calls for the roll call vote. The anti-Duterte faction sweeps all 11 of their votes to convict. The remaining 9 pro-Duterte senators vote to acquit.

😯The final tally on the floor reads: 11 to Convict, 9 to Acquit.

👍🏽The anti-Duterte faction celebrates on the floor, claiming a majority victory of those present. However, the Senate Secretary-General stands up to read the constitutional mandate: Article XI, Section 3 of the Constitution requires two-thirds of all the members, which means a hard, unyielding target of 16 votes.

👍🏽Because 11 is less than 16, Vice President Sara Duterte is officially acquitted. The arrest of the 4 senators inadvertently seals her survival because it freezes the voting math without lowering the constitutional bar.

👉🏽The Explosive Political Aftermath

If this scenario played out, it would trigger a massive constitutional and social crisis in Manila:

🟥The "Weaponized Justice" Backlash: The public and international observers would instantly view the arrests of the 4 senators right before a crucial vote as a desperate, weaponized political hit by the administration. This would turn the arrested senators into political martyrs and heavily boost VP Sara's narrative of being a victim of persecution.

🟥The Supreme Court Showdown: The anti-Duterte bloc would immediately file a petition with the Supreme Court, arguing that "all members" should mean "all functioning members" (reducing the pool to 20 senators, making 14 votes the new two-thirds threshold). The pro-Duterte bloc would counter with strict constitutional text. The Supreme Court would likely rule in favor of the strict 16-vote interpretation to prevent future administrations from simply arresting opponents to win votes.

🟥Total Senate Gridlock: Following the trial, the remaining 9 pro-Duterte senators would likely alliance with unaligned senators to form a devastating 10-to-11 member voting bloc. They would refuse to grant a quorum for normal legislative work, effectively paralyzing the administration's legislative agenda for the remainder of the year.

AN OPEN LETTER TO DENR SECRETARY JUAN MIGUEL CUNA

An Appeal to the Conscious Stewardship of our Urban Canopy and Climate Future

To: The Honorable Juan Miguel T. Cuna Acting Secretary, Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) @DENROfficial 

Visayas Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City

CC: @TanggolKalikasn, @gpph, @EcoWastePH, @KalikasanPNE, @WWF, @GoHaribon 

Dear Secretary Cuna,

We write this as citizens, taxpayers, and residents of a rapidly warming National Capital Region, deeply alarmed by the state-sanctioned destruction of approximately 600 mature shade trees along Quirino Avenue in Manila to make way for the Southern Access Link Expressway (SALEX).

In a recent press briefing, you defended this massive clearing operation by stating, "Walang may gustong magputol ng puno," and remarked, "this is the world that we live in right now," pointing to the principles of sustainable development.

With all due respect, Mr. Secretary, the world we live in right now is one of breaking heat records, severe climate vulnerability, and intensifying urban heat islands. Deforesting the few remaining "green lungs" of our capital city to accommodate more vehicle infrastructure is a direct contradiction of the very sustainability you invoked.

True sustainable development meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Stripping Manila of mature, decades-old tree canopies fails this definition on multiple fronts:

The Illusion of the 1:85 Replacement Ratio: While the DENR mandates thousands of saplings to replace these mature trees, a sapling planted elsewhere cannot replicate the immediate, life-saving ecological services of a 30-year-old tree. Saplings do not absorb particulate air pollution, mitigate severe flooding, or shield commuters from 45°C heat indexes today when the community needs it most.

Aggravating the Urban Heat Crisis: Removing these trees strips away natural cooling mechanisms, directly worsening the microclimate and increasing thermal discomfort for ordinary commuters, jeepney drivers, vendors, and residents who have no choice but to navigate these streets.

Prioritizing Car Infrastructure Over People: Car-centric infrastructure like SALEX exacerbates induced demand bringing more traffic and higher emissions while destroying the natural infrastructure that protects public health.

As a former councilor of Manila’s 5th District, you know these streets and these communities intimately. You know that Manila is starving for green spaces, not concrete overheads. As a lawyer trained in development and public policy, you know that the state’s primary mandate under Section 16, Article II of the Constitution is to protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology.

No one wants to cut down trees, yet the permits bear your department's signature. If "this is the world we live in," then let it be a world where the primary environmental regulatory body draws a hard line against ecological regression.

We urgently call on the DENR to:

- Issue a Status Quo Ante Order or an immediate moratorium on any further tree-cutting and earth-balling along the SALEx project corridor.

- Conduct a transparent, independent review of the project's Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) and hold a genuine, public consultation with affected residents and urban planning experts.

- Compel project proponents to redesign infrastructure around existing natural ecosystems, rather than erasing nature for convenience.

Development that costs us our breath, our shade, and our climate resilience is not development at all—it is a deficit we cannot afford. We look to your leadership to steer the DENR back toward genuine, unyielding environmental stewardship.

Respectfully yours,

Concerned Citizens 
for a Green and Resilient Manila
